content.thinking:
I need to write the whole file carefully in one pass. Since the builder requires a root joint even for simple props, I'll create a base root joint at the origin to satisfy that requirement before adding the rest of the parts.

With that structure settled, I'm sketching a bookshelf roughly 1.2m wide, 0.4m deep, and 2m tall, with side panels, an arched crown top, a plinth base, a back panel, and four shelves positioned at increasing heights. I'm planning helper functions for boxes with position/rotation options, using toon-style cel colors and wood grain textures for materials, and designing a book-generating helper that builds spine-facing covers and page blocks with varying thickness, height, depth, and tilt to populate the shelves realistically.

Each book is assembled from a pages block plus thin cover boards and a spine with decorative gold bands and a small label, keeping part counts manageable across roughly 40 books while staying well under the total part budget. I'm also starting to think through small decorative orbs with stands and glowing inner spheres to scatter around the scene.

Candles get cream cylinders with drip details, wicks, and glowing flame cones sitting in gold lathe holders, placed on shelves and in a candelabra; scrolls become horizontal parchment-colored cylinders with ribbon ties and wooden knobs, with stacks arranged in a pigeonhole cubby rack oriented along the z-axis.

For the crown, I'm planning gold filigree with an arched wooden silhouette and a crescent moon cutout built from two offset arcs so the shape reads cleanly without self-intersecting, with the opening facing outward.

I'm solving for the actual intersection points of the two circles to get precise angles for the crescent's outer and inner arcs, rather than guessing endpoint coordinates.

Checking the inner arc stays non-intersecting with the outer at its narrowest point, which looks fine. Now I'm planning the shelf structure: side panels as painted boxes with grain along y, gold edge strips on the front faces, and considering pilasters or vertical trim details on the front sides.

I'm sketching the cornice at the top, then a crown arch extruded above it using a curved outline profile, bringing the total unit height to roughly 2.3 meters. I'll add a crescent moon ornament on the crown front in gold with small glowing stars, then move on to designing the base plinth.

Working out the interior shelf layout: defining shelf board heights, panel thicknesses, and interior width so the cabinet's internal structure lines up cleanly beneath the cornice.

I'm giving the back panel a decorative starry-sky texture via an SVG decal—dark indigo gradient with stars and a gold rune circle—mapped onto a thin plane facing forward inside the cabinet.

Now I'm adding a thin gold trim strip along each shelf edge, then laying out the first shelf's contents: stacked and standing books on the left, leaving room for an orb on a stand on the right, with careful depth positioning so items sit forward of the painted back panel and recessed behind the shelf lip.

For the second shelf, I'm placing standing books on the left and designing a small 3x2 pigeonhole scroll rack with dividers on the right side, sizing the cubbies and verifying the whole assembly fits within the shelf's vertical clearance.

Building the open book prop...

For shelf 3, I'm planning candles flanking the sides, books centered, and an armillary sphere as the focal point—a glowing orb wrapped in gold torus rings mounted on a stand.

Up top on the cornice, I'll place candelabra on either side of the crown ornament plus a bundled scroll, skipping decorative extras like an owl. On the floor beside the shelf, I'm adding clutter—a stack of tomes with a melted candle and leaning scroll on the right, and a small glowing orb resting on a cushion to the left, keeping the overall spread within about two meters wide.

Now I'm settling on a color palette: warm and dark wood tones, cel-shaded gold, parchment, and a varied set of book cover colors like crimson, royal blue, emerald, purple, teal, orange, ivory, and midnight. I'm planning to shade each book cover using cel paints based on face normals rather than individual textures, adding gold spine bands and randomizing book height and thickness for natural variation.

I'm designing a book-building function that takes position, dimensions, cover color, and an optional lean angle, using a local-to-world coordinate helper so each part (spine, cover, label) rotates correctly around the book's base pivot when tilted.

Setting up imports and checking types to avoid unused-import errors before writing the module.

Adding more helper functions...

Now I'm setting up the color palette with named materials for wood grain, dark tones, gold accents, parchment, and glowing highlights.

I'm writing a book-building function that positions pages and cover with a tilt rotation, handling ornate details as a parameter.

Writing book geometry...

Still writing book geometry code...

Working out the leaning book geometry...

Now I'm figuring out shelf board positions and clearances, setting board tops at 0.12, 0.58, 1.02, and 1.44 with roughly 0.46 clearance for each shelf section accounting for the 0.03 board thickness.

I'm also working out depth placement for books and the back panel, checking that the book depth and shelf board depth don't overlap awkwardly with the back wall texture.

Now I'm sketching the candle holder geometry, using a lathe profile to create a small gold dish shape that the candle will sit in.

Still writing candle components...

Positioning the orb above the stand, I'm adding four gold claw prongs around it using spike rods angled outward, then giving the orb itself a glowing textured surface—an SVG radial gradient with teal swirls and sparkles to make it feel magical rather than flat.

Positioning the highlight so it protrudes slightly looks right. Now I'm setting up the armillary rings using torus geometry with different rotations to give that classic orbital-sphere look, then moving on to the scroll element.

For the scroll, I'm defining a cylinder shape with wooden rod ends and ball caps, plus a red ribbon wrapped around it as a cylindrical band at an offset along its length.

For the end faces, I'm using a circular plane textured with an SVG spiral pattern — parchment-colored fill with a concentric spiral stroke — positioned at the front of each scroll facing outward, since only one end needs to be visible.

Now I'm designing the potion bottle using a lathe geometry for the glass body with a glowing purple material, plus a brown cork cylinder and a small cream label. For the open book on the stand, I'm thinking through a simple wooden lectern shape to hold it upright on the shelf.

I'm positioning text planes just above each page's surface, tilted to match the page normal, and giving the right page a glowing gold/cyan rune circle while keeping the left page's text as plain ink. I'll skip the bookmark ribbon for now but may add gold corner accents to the cover.

For the back panel, I'm generating a starry-night texture with a gradient background, randomly placed stars, faint gold constellation lines, and a rune-marked circle motif—most of it hidden behind shelves but peeking through near the top. Then I'm extruding an arched crown shape above the cornice to cap the structure.

Defining crown outline points...

Still designing the crescent moon shape...

Placing the moon within the arch opening, I'm now adding cornice details—a dentil row of small gold boxes under the cornice, plus layered molding boxes for the cornice cap, working out the vertical bands so they stack cleanly without overlap.

Still positioning finials and dentils...

I'm also thinking about adding gold vertical strips and decorative plane textures on the side panel faces, like a vine or rune pattern on the outer surface, to add visual richness without too much geometry.

Then I'm sketching the plinth base: a dark box with gold trim and a top molding piece, working out the exact vertical positions so it sits flush on the floor without overlapping the shelf board beneath it.

Next I'm adding a thin gold molding strip along the shelf's front edge, then deciding to skip extra details like hanging tassels or ribbons to keep things simple. I'm now planning the concrete book arrangement shelf by shelf, starting with the bottom shelf's leaning and standing book rows.

Still placing shelf objects...

Laying out shelf one with a leaning row, then designing the scroll rack with vertical divider boards and horizontal shelf boxes to form three cubbies within the frame.

Checking clearances above the rack against the next shelf up, and sizing the scroll radii so each cubby can fit one scroll comfortably, adjusting cubby center positions to match the board thicknesses.

I'm thinking about adding small brass tag boxes under the dividers as labels, then moving on to the second shelf layout with a leaning row of books and an open book placed near the center.

For the open book area I'm placing potion bottles of varying heights alongside a small purple orb on a mini stand, scaling the stand proportionally to the orb's radius. Then I'm moving on to the third shelf, starting with a tall brass candlestick built from a lathed stand profile topped with a candle.

Working out the center orb's position: with radius 0.12 the stand height comes to about 0.1, placing the top around 1.76, and the armillary ring fits within 1.8, staying clear of the book rows on either side. For the cornice top I'm placing a three-candle candelabra on the left and a stack of flat books with a candle on the right, possibly adding a scroll lying across the top.

Switching idea: instead of the book stack, I'm adding a whimsical wizard hat on the top right with a brim and tapered cone, finished with a gold buckle ring and a deep purple color.

Checking placement, I realize the hat brim would collide with the crown's decorative arch at this x-position, so I need to shift the hat further right, but that risks pushing it off the shelf edge entirely.

I'll make the crown narrower by rescaling its outline points, which frees up space at x=0.32..0.6 for the hat without overlap, while keeping the candelabra on the left clear. I'm also verifying the moon ornament fits within the crown's width at its vertical position.

Now I'm positioning two stars near the crown's base where it's wide enough, then building the candelabra: a lathed stem profile plus three arms extending from the stem to hold candles of varying heights.

Adding thin rods for the arms with a center candle on top, using candle geometry that includes a dish catcher. Then I'm scattering floor clutter—stacked books and an orb cushion on one side, book piles and a candle on the other—plus sketching a woven basket shape via a lathed shell profile to hold scrolls leaning against the shelf.

For the right floor, I'm adding a book pile with a candle on top and wax drips, plus an oval rug underneath with an ornate carpet-pattern texture rendered as a textured plane facing upward.

The rug overlaps the shelf plinth area slightly but that's fine since it's covered by the plinth base. Floor clutter items like the basket and pile sit at z=0.5, positioned in front of the shelf rather than against it, so no leaning needed. I'm sketching the rug as an SVG ellipse with gold rings and a diamond pattern instead of tassels, sized to a 1.9x0.95 plane with a matching viewBox ratio.

I decide to skip the ladder and cobweb ideas since they'd clutter or hide the books, and drop hanging tassel cards too, keeping just simple ribbons. I verify the rug's orientation math checks out with the plane normal and axis alignment, then start tallying up book counts per shelf to estimate total part counts for the scene.

I work through the math: with roughly 25-30 books per shelf at 8 parts each (pages, boards, spines, bands, label), the total lands around 450-500 parts, which stays safely under budget, and box geometries at 12 triangles each keep the triangle count manageable too. Now I'm defining the flatBook helper function, setting up its local axes with width along x and depth along z, figuring out spine orientation for stacked books facing forward.

Defining book part dimensions...

Writing orb texture gradient...

Adding scattered stars, constellation lines, and a gold rune circle with inner pentagram...

Now I'm designing a side vine texture panel with a sine-wave vine and leaf details, then positioning mirrored decorative planes on the left and right sides of the panel at the correct depth and orientation.

I'm skipping extra embellishments like gem glow or bookends for simplicity, and focusing on writing a typed box helper function that creates geometry parts with configurable size, color, position, and rotation, defaulting to identity rotation.

Now I'm defining helper functions for cylinders with optional direction, and a candle function using a lathe geometry with an outline of points to shape the wax profile.

Writing dish and flame outline coordinates...

Now I'm setting flame glow colors and thinking through wax drips as scaled ellipsoid spheres, then starting a helper function to build an orb mesh with optional rings, scaled relative to a base radius.

Working out prong positions around the orb's sphere surface...

Still writing part definitions...

Still placing scroll details...

I'll put spiral end caps on both ends of the scroll for a lying-down look, using two parchment paint variants for variety, then move on to building the potion bottle with a lathed glass body, cork, label, and gold neck ring.

Now I'm designing an open book: a red cover, slightly rotated left and right page slabs, a cylindrical spine hump, and tilted text planes positioned over each page to simulate writing.

The glow rune uses a cyan stroke with a glow effect, while the ink lines stay matte. I'm skipping ribbon bookmarks, confirming the plane's up-vector for the tilt, and now defining the ten cover colors—crimson, cobalt, emerald, violet, teal, amber, plum, forest, navy, ivory—each as its own paint applied per book cel.

Painted textures look fine, with gold bands handled as flat paint, and I'm confirming the paint sheet resolution and seeding the RNG for the build. Now I'm writing the crescent shape function, generating outer and inner arc points via trigonometry and rotating the result.

Checking the angle math confirms the inner arc correctly traces through 180 degrees, carving out the crescent shape between the outer and inner circle boundaries, and verifying the polygon closes properly at the endpoints.

Now I'm defining the star outline with alternating inner/outer radius points starting at 90 degrees, then setting up extrude parameters: thin bevels for the star geometry and a separate extrude for the crown shape with dark coloring positioned above the main form.

For the crown's trim detail, I'm sweeping a thin gold tube along the arch outline points, running from one bottom edge up over the apex to the other side, leaving the bottom open and letting the tube radius naturally smooth the corners.

Now I'm positioning the side panels as boxes spanning roughly y=0.1 to 1.9, matching the cornice height, with a back panel and texture plane sized similarly. For the wood grain, I need separate paint variants with grain running along different axes—one for sides using a horizontal grain variant, keeping the vertical-grain version for other boards.

Assigning darker finishes to the back panel and plinth, then adding gold trim strips and small glowing teal gem spheres spaced along the side panels for ornamentation. Now I'm defining a helper function to generate rows of these decorative elements.

Checking the corner math confirms the tilted book only sinks slightly below the shelf line, and the rightward offset still stays within the bound, so the lean fits safely within the available space with random depth variation for each book.

I'm also adding front-aligned z-depth jitter for the row books, then laying out a floor book pile with varying heights, widths, and rotations, plus a candle stacked on top at the right height.

For shelf zero I'm centering a second stack of flat books near x=0.0, adjusting width so it doesn't overlap the row that ends around -0.18, and placing an orb nearby around x=0.33.

Now checking the orb's stand radius against the stack's right edge and the row's placement on the right side, confirming there's enough clearance for two books without leaning.

For shelf one I'm working out the rack divider positions and spacing, making sure the leaning book in the row has enough room before the row's end, then calculating cubby centers and radii for the scrolls based on the divider x-coordinates.

I'm figuring out vertical placement for the scrolls in each cubby, computing centers for lower and upper rows based on the shelf and mid-board heights, checking that cubby clearance exceeds the scroll diameter, and considering splitting some cubbies into paired smaller scrolls side by side.

I'm positioning small brass tag boxes at the front edge of each shelf's mid and top boards, then laying out the next shelf's row coordinates.

For shelf 2, I'm placing the open book, potions at varying heights, and a tiny orb on its stand, checking each item fits within the shelf width.

For shelf 3, I'm planning tall candlesticks near the shelf edges and starting a lathe profile for the candlestick shape.

Still writing lathe coordinates for the candle...

Still shaping the hat cone...

Adding a gold buckle band and checking the hat's height clears the crown without colliding with the cornice.

Now I'm designing a floor basket with a lathe profile for the wicker body plus a gold torus rim, positioning it near the rug.

For the scrolls leaning out of the basket, I'm computing five tilted directions with slightly varied base offsets so each scroll's base sits inside the basket radius while its length tilts outward through the center point — checking that geometry works out before moving on to rug texture details.

I'm designing the rug as an SVG with a deep red elliptical base, a gold ring border, a navy inner ellipse, gold diamond patterns, and a central medallion with a star, sized up for a 1024px texture. I'm also tallying up texture resolutions across all the elements—background, side panels, rug, spiral, text, runes, and orbs—to keep the atlas organized before assembling everything.

Writing cylinder helper function...

Still writing geometry helpers...

Now I'm finalizing details like the highlight glow and background circle styling, then moving on to writing the metadata and committing the final output carefully.
